name: Supreme London
why: Supreme's first European store (2011), with Mark Gonzales artwork on the walls. Thursday drops mean weekends are calmer.

name: Palace Skateboards
why: London's own skate brand in its hometown flagship, so there's stock you won't see in LA.

name: Stüssy London Chapter
why: Cali brand, but the London Chapter store gets its own city-exclusive tees.

name: Aimé Leon Dore
why: ALD's only European store. The Adolf Loos-inspired interior is worth seeing even if you don't buy.

name: END. London
why: Big multi-brand flagship: Stone Island, sneaker wall, lots of labels in one stop.

name: Footpatrol
why: London's best-known sneaker shop, known for collabs and London-only releases.

name: Kith London (+ Ronnie's)
why: 19,000 sq ft UK flagship, opened Nov 2025, with Kith Treats and Ronnie Fieg's own restaurant inside.

name: Dover Street Market
why: Comme des Garçons' six-floor concept store with Nike, Stüssy and ERL sitting next to high fashion. The art installations alone make it worth a visit.

name: Carhartt WIP
why: Big Seven Dials store with European WIP colourways.

name: Nike London (Oxford Circus)
why: Nike's huge flagship with London-specific product and customisation.

name: Selfridges
why: 8 min walk from the Airbnb. The designer menswear and sneaker floors are good, and the Foodhall is great for a quick bite.

name: Goodhood
why: East London's big independent concept store (moved to Hanbury St in 2024). Well-curated menswear and homeware.

name: Beyond Retro (Cheshire St)
why: Massive warehouse of vintage: sportswear, varsity jackets, workwear, all off Brick Lane.

name: Brick Lane Vintage Market
address: Old Truman Brewery, 85 Brick Lane, London E1 6QL
why: Dozens of vintage traders under one roof, with sportswear and 90s gear.

name: The Vintage Showroom
why: Serious vintage menswear (military, workwear, denim). A small shop across from Carhartt.

name: Rough Trade East
address: Old Truman Brewery, 91 Brick Lane, London E1 6QL
why: The legendary record shop's big east London outpost, with regular free in-store gigs.

name: Sister Ray
why: The West End's biggest indie record shop, next door to Footpatrol. Berwick St is the Oasis 'What's the Story' album cover street.

name: Phonica Records
why: London's go-to electronic/dance vinyl shop, with listening stations.

name: Ronnie Scott's
why: World-famous jazz club since 1959. The late show is a great post-dinner move. Book ahead.

name: Abbey Road crossing
why: The Beatles album-cover crossing. It's a real road, so time the photo between cars.

name: Roundhouse
why: Iconic Camden venue (the Doors and Hendrix played there). Check what's on.

name: fabric
why: London's most famous club. Friday and Saturday nights only, so book tickets ahead.

name: Borough Market
why: London's best food market, 1,000 years old. Kappacasein toasted cheese sandwich, Bread Ahead doughnuts. Closes 16:00 Sunday.

name: Padella
why: Cult fresh-pasta spot. Join the virtual queue and wander the market while you wait.

name: Maltby Street Market
why: Street food under railway arches: smaller and less touristy than Borough, 10 min from Tower Bridge.

name: Dishoom Carnaby
why: Bombay-café comfort food. The bacon naan roll at breakfast and the black daal are must-orders. Expect a queue at peak times.

name: Dishoom Shoreditch
why: Same Dishoom classics in a big Shoreditch space with a verandah. Great for a Sunday brunch.

name: Beigel Bake
why: 24/7 institution: the salt beef bagel with mustard is ~£8 and legendary. Cash is easiest.

name: BAO Soho
why: Taiwanese steamed buns. Fast, cheap-ish, and a good way to reset mid-shopping.

name: Flat Iron (Beak St)
why: Very good steak for about £15, plus free ice cream. Best value sit-down in Soho for a group of 5.

name: Bar Italia
why: Soho's late-night espresso bar since 1949 (the Pulp song). Good for a post-night-out stop.

name: Tayyabs
why: Punjabi grill famous for lamb chops. BYO drinks, loud and cheap.

name: The Golden Hind
why: Proper fish & chips since 1914, 10 min walk from the Airbnb.

name: Paul Rothe & Son
why: Family deli since 1900. Old-school sandwiches, a quick breakfast before the airport.

name: Selfridges Foodhall
why: Grab-and-go counters inside Selfridges. Close to home and good for when the group can't agree.

name: Westfield Stratford City
why: Right between Stratford station and the stadium. Food court and bars for pre-match food or to wait out the post-match crush.
verified: landmark; restaurants open later than shops

name: BFI IMAX
why: The UK's biggest cinema screen. Catch whatever's showing in IMAX 70mm if you can.

name: Prince Charles Cinema
why: Cult cinema off Leicester Sq: sing-alongs, 35/70mm prints and all-nighters. Check what's on.

name: Leadenhall Market (Diagon Alley)
why: Victorian covered market used as Diagon Alley in Harry Potter. Quick photo stop.

name: Platform 9¾, King's Cross
why: Harry Potter trolley photo op (queue can be long).

name: Huntsman, Savile Row (Kingsman)
why: The real tailor that inspired the Kingsman shop. Walk Savile Row for the vibe.

name: Millennium Bridge
why: The bridge Death Eaters destroy in Half-Blood Prince, with St Paul's framed at the end.

name: The Globe Tavern (Bridget Jones)
why: Pub under Bridget Jones's flat, next door to OMA. A good pre-dinner pint.

name: Sherlock Holmes Museum (221b)
why: 15 min walk from the Airbnb. The shopfront photo is enough; skip the queue.

name: The Notting Hill Bookshop
why: The bookshop from Notting Hill, just off Portobello Road.

name: Emirates Stadium Tour (Arsenal)
why: Dressing rooms, tunnel and pitchside. Hours listed are last entry; no tours on home match days. About £35, book on arsenal.com.

name: Stamford Bridge Tour (Chelsea FC)
why: Chelsea's stadium tour and museum, 20 min walk from Kutir. No tours on Sat 10 Oct (match day); Sunday or Monday works. Book ahead.

name: BOX Piccadilly
why: Official NFL UK partner bar with big screens and sound. Where to watch Sunday's games.

name: Passyunk Avenue (Fitzrovia)
why: American sports bar (Philly cheesesteaks, every NFL/NBA game). A slice of home.

name: Big Ben & Parliament
why: Best photo is from Westminster Bridge. Loop to the Abbey in 2 min.

name: Westminster Abbey
why: Coronation church. Outside is free; inside is ~£30 and takes an hour, so the exterior is enough for most.

name: Buckingham Palace
why: Walk up the Mall from Trafalgar Sq through St James's Park. Changing of the Guard is ~11:00 on set days.

name: Trafalgar Square
why: Lions, fountains, National Gallery (free) behind. Connects Soho to Westminster.

name: London Eye
why: 30 min ride with the best skyline view. Pre-book or it's a long queue.

name: Southbank Skatepark (Undercroft)
address: Southbank Centre, Belvedere Road, London SE1 8XX
why: Birthplace of UK skate culture, covered in graffiti. Palace's roots are here.

name: Tate Modern
why: Free modern art in a power station. The Turbine Hall installation and the 10th-floor viewing level are the highlights.

name: Tower Bridge
why: Walk across for free. The glass floor walkway is paid (~£13) if you want it.

name: Tower of London
why: Crown Jewels and Beefeaters. A 2-hour commitment, so outside photos may be enough.

name: Sky Garden
why: Free 35th-floor garden with 360° views. You need a free booking online (released ~3 weeks ahead).

name: St Paul's Cathedral
why: Wren's dome. Cross the Millennium Bridge to reach Tate Modern.

name: Hyde Park & Speakers' Corner
why: Right by the Airbnb. A quick walk to reset between plans.

name: The Wallace Collection
address: Hertford House, Manchester Square, London W1U 3BN
why: Free: armour, Old Masters, a gorgeous courtyard. 7 min from the Airbnb.

name: Camden Market
why: Vintage, street food and punk history by the canal.

name: Portobello Road Market
why: Saturday is the big antiques + vintage day; the Golborne Road end has the best vintage clothing.

name: Old Spitalfields Market
why: Covered market with indie designers and food stalls, 2 min from Brick Lane.

name: Boxpark Shoreditch
why: Shipping-container food and bars with big screens for sport, by Shoreditch High St station.

name: Brick Lane street art
address: Brick Lane / Hanbury St / Grimsby St, London E1
why: Walls change constantly. Hanbury St, Fashion St and Grimsby St are the best side streets.

name: King's Road
why: The Sex Pistols-era punk street, now nice shops. It walks straight to Kutir.

name: Saatchi Gallery
address: Duke of York's HQ, King's Road, London SW3 4RY
why: Contemporary art, often free, 3 min from Kutir. An ideal pre-dinner time-filler.
